<reason>PRO won a close debate by keeping the motion’s modest burden live: space tourism still needs a justification while climate harm and severe poverty persist. The opening triad (stratospheric intensity, scarce aerospace inputs, tourism ≠ useful spaceflight) plus the rarity/scale fork left CON’s industrial-benefit story looking either too small to matter or large enough to reopen the climate ledger. CON was more careful, refused fake thresholds, and used polar cruises to show PRO’s “beyond the buyer” test is fuzzier than advertised; after PRO bit the luxury bullet, that consistency hit no longer killed the motion as written. CON’s remaining case was a general no-standing-veto theory and “the passenger pays,” which never fully discharged the trade the proposition asks about. PRO overclaimed uniqueness and clipped a speech, so the edge is real but competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s R1 fork ([B2.1]–[B2.2]): CON cannot call tourism a climate rounding error and the thing that amortizes reusable flight rates. CON’s different-scales reply ([A2.1], [A4.1]) was the best answer, but “tens of flights” left the public-benefit story too thin.</best_rebuttal>
